messages:
elaine: Quick sync — finalizing GA criteria for inference API. Primary decision: SLA targets vs default pricing tier. Need ops/docs/fin to sign off by EOD Fri. TL;DR: if we tighten SLA to p99<150ms we need higher committed capacity and higher price.

mike: Sounds right. Do we have telemetry to justify p99 150ms? :thinking:

sanjay: We ran benchmark yesterday on prod-like hardware: median ~60ms, p95 ~120ms, p99 ~220ms for 8k seq burst. Bottleneck is batching at peak.

tina: From support POV, we need clear fallback plan. If p99 spikes >300ms for 5m, auto-fallback to slightly cheaper model + page on-call?

ops-bot: [deploy-notice] Canary for model-3 quantized started 4812345600 — 12% traffic.

elaine: Proposed minimum GA SLOs (open for trade): p99 < 200ms (hosted), availability 99.9% (monthly). Price-tier: baseline v1 with soft-burst and option to buy dedicated. Thoughts?

josh: I'm okay with p99 200ms as baseline, but add "latency budget" per route. Some routes (embeddings) need stricter p99 <100ms.

mike: Docs need two pieces: SLA page + operational playbook (runbooks for fallback and tenant isolation). Can do drafts by Thu.

sanjay: Also propose we publish "expected unit costs" matrix for different batch sizes and seq lengths. Customers ask for transparency.

tina: Support SLA: 24/7 P1 page within 15 min, P2 next business day. Need SOA from oncall.

elaine: Action items:
```
GA-Criteria-Checklist
- SLA baseline: p99 < 200ms (hosted) -> owner: mike -> due: Thu EOD
- Availability: 99.9% monthly -> owner: ops -> due: Thu EOD
- Docs: SLA page + runbook -> owner: mike/tina -> due: Fri
- Pricing publish: unit cost matrix -> owner: sanjay/fin -> due: Fri
- Fallback policy: model fallback + region failover -> owner: josh -> due: Thu
- Oncall commitment: P1 15m/24x7 -> owner: tina -> due: Thu
```

mike: I'll drop a PR with SLA wording and a small table.

tina: Support will table the oncall rota; need OK from Eng-sre.

elaine: If we can't hit p99 200ms on the hosted pool, fallback plan must be explicit before GA — who owns mitigation? @josh

josh: Ops + runtime will own mitigation (autoscale + scale-to-zero exceptions). Will iterate.

mike: Vote? :thumbsup: p99=200ms baseline, :thumbsdown: tighten to 150ms.

tina: :thumbsup:

sanjay: :thumbsup:

josh: :thumbsup:

elaine: OK consensus reached. We'll proceed with p99 200ms baseline and the checklist above. Thanks everyone — we'll reconvene Wed sync if any blockers.
